key_insight: An identical-material tracer inserted into AA5083 enabled direct, quantitative mapping of strain heterogeneity in the friction stir weld nugget, revealing distinct shoulder-, compressive-, and pin-dominated deformation zones.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a physically representative way to measure local strain during FSW, helping link process conditions to grain refinement and weld microstructure.
method: Embedded anodized AA5083 foil tracer inside AA5083 base metal
Performed FSW at 1025 rpm and 67 mm/min
Used tracer deformation and thickness reduction to estimate local strain; confirmed microstructure with EBSD
evidence_signal: The abstract reports peak strains of about 2.0 in the shoulder-affected zone, 0.4 in compression, and 1.1 in the pin-affected zone, with grain size refining from 13.0 ± 4.2 µm to 5.0 ± 1.8 µm and high-angle grain boundaries rising from 68.5% to 89.3%.
watch_item: The strain field is inferred from tracer deformation, so accuracy may depend on tracer placement, sectioning quality, and whether the foil truly follows local material flow without disturbing it.
paper_title: Experimental measurement of strain distribution in the nugget zone during friction stir welding using an identical-material tracer
